extracted.intended_audience: zoologists, naturalists, taxonomists and students compiling or using faunal lists of freshwater sponges, hydroids, and polyzoa (India/Burma/Ceylon) and general readers of natural-history monographs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and conventions for assembling and presenting a geographical/faunal list of freshwater sponges, hydroids, and polyzoa (with scope notes on brackish/stagnant-water forms), and the distribution-annotation conventions used in the volume. Includes Project Gutenberg redistribution/license requirements for the eBook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical symbol notation for species lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotation symbols used in the geographical list: 'A * indicates that a species or subspecies has only been found in one physiographical region or subregion so far as the Indian Empire is concerned; a ! that the species has also been found in Europe, a $ in North America, a + in Africa, and a @ in the Malay Archipelago.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These symbols are applied throughout the geographical list to indicate known extra-Indian or regionally restricted occurrences; they should be placed alongside species entries to summarise distribution at a glance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of varieties from geographical list
rubrics_metrics.description: "'Varieties' are ignored in this list, because they are not considered to have a geographical significance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When compiling the distribution list, do not treat named varieties as separate geographic records — they are omitted because they are not judged to carry meaningful geographic significance for the catalogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of regional framework: physiographical regions
rubrics_metrics.description: The geographical list is modelled on Col. Alcock's list and the author follows Blanford's physiographical rather than his zoogeographical regions for delimiting areas of the Indian Empire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For freshwater invertebrates the author prefers physiographical regions (landform/climatic/physiography-based divisions) as the primary spatial units for distribution statements, with minor modifications as needed; use those regions consistently when assigning locality records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: include freshwater forms and selected stagnant brackish-water species
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the volume deals mainly with freshwater species, the author explicitly includes the freshwater representatives of sponges, coelenterates, and polyzoa and, in introductions to each part, provides a list of species found in stagnant brackish water with notes and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main list focuses on freshwater occurrences, but where relevant (especially for estuarine or stagnant brackish pools) include brackish-water species with brief notes and bibliographic references rather than full treatment; be explicit about scope limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for inclusion: specimen records and literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Species and localities in the list are reported based on collected specimens (museum/field records) and the published literature; the author notes gaps in knowledge for certain regions and highlights where records are sparse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include locality information and, where applicable, citation or collector information; note uncertain or single-record occurrences and acknowledge geographic sampling gaps rather than treating absence as evidence of true absence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a standardised explanatory preface for special localities
rubrics_metrics.description: The author supplies a short, standardised account of frequently mentioned localities (e.g., Lower Bengal, Calcutta tanks, Malabar Zone) to avoid repetition and to provide context about habitat and collecting conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When many entries refer to the same localities, provide a single descriptive note summarising habitat, typical substrates, and collecting biases to contextualise distributional records.
